newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share prices climb despite budget.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share prices climb despite budget.

text.p: Shares rose on the Nigerian stock exchange on Monday in spite of traders' regrets that the military government's 1997 budget put privatisation on hold.
The all-share index closed at 7122.10 from 7096.39 on Friday.
"There may be dissapointment over privatisation, but in the short term there is nothing in the budget to change equity prices one way or the other on the day," said one trader.
Investors rushed to buy shares in First Bank after a technical hold on its price was removed following the listing of shares from a recent sale, traders said.
It gained the maximum five percent, closing 35 kobo up at 7.45 naira on positive perception.
Afribank went eight kobo higher at 3.70 naira and United Bank for Africa closed at 7.00 naira, 25 kobo stronger.
Relative scarcity of petroleum marketing shares continued to push their prices higher.
Total went 70 kobo higher at 61.00 naira, Unipetrol was 40 kobo up at 63.00 naira and Mobil closed 45 kobo better at 53.00 naira amid undiminished demand.
Union Dicon Salt climbed 65 kobo to 44.00 naira 65 kobo while Nestle rose 35 kobo to 52.00 naira.
Union Bank and John Holt went ex-dividend, shedding 50 kobo to close at 6.35 naira and 30 kobo to end at 9.70 naira respectively.
Leading conglomerate Lever Brothers fell 25 kobo to 18.75 naira with a glut of shares on the floor.
Chemical and Allied Products slid 10 kobo to 4.90 naira while African Paints closed two kobo down at 1.60 naira.
Paper company Thomas Wyatt fell five kobo to 6.25 naira and textile group Afprint, hit by a recent fire at one of its subsidiaries, shed four kobo to close at 2.55 naira.
